removed_items.title: The coherence type over a right inverse of a half adjoint equivalence is contractible
removed_items.author: The Univalent Foundations Program
removed_items.work: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics
removed_items.source_version: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics source tree, file equivalences.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
removed_items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source lines 351-353 (book Lemma 4.2.12): if f is a half adjoint equivalence then for every right inverse with its homotopy the coherence type over that pair is contractible. The statement is a contractibility claim about data attached to a pair, and the proof (source lines 354-357) has to first replace the coherence type by a dependent product of path types inside the fibers, which is what makes it possible to argue pointwise, and then to notice that the fiber of a half adjoint equivalence is contractible so that each required path space is contractible as well. The reduction of the coherence datum to a pointwise path statement is the content and the statement shows none of it.

removed_items.title: The half adjoint equivalence structure on a map is a mere proposition
removed_items.author: The Univalent Foundations Program
removed_items.work: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics
removed_items.source_version: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics source tree, file equivalences.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
removed_items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled theorem at source lines 359-361 (book Theorem 4.2.13): for every map f the type of half adjoint equivalence structures on f is a mere proposition. The statement is a propositionality claim about a nested structure, and the proof (source lines 362-367) has to choose the right reduction: it first turns propositionality into contractibility under an assumed inhabitant, then rewrites the structure by associativity of the Sigma type so that the coherence datum is taken at the right inverse rather than at the inverse map, and only then can it invoke the two contractibility results and the closure of contractibility under Sigma types. Which component the structure should be flattened at, and why that is the right choice, is exactly what the statement does not show.

removed_items.author: The Univalent Foundations Program
removed_items.work: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics
removed_items.source_version: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics source tree, file equivalences.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
removed_items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled theorem at source lines 447-449 (book Theorem 4.4.3): for every map f, contractibility of its fibers implies that it is a half adjoint equivalence. The statement is an implication between two structures and the proof (source lines 450-458) has to construct each piece of the target structure from the hypothesis: the inverse map is the first component of a center of contraction, the homotopy is the witness that this point lies in the fiber, and the coherence datum, which is where the real work is, is first reduced through the cited lemma to a path inside a fiber and then produced explicitly from the contraction of that fiber as a concatenation of the two contraction paths. The reduction of the coherence to a path in a fiber, and the choice of its two endpoints, are invisible in the statement.

The proof (source lines 484-487) is short but it is the reduction itself and not a pointer: it moves to the fibre criterion, fixes an arbitrary point of the codomain, applies the assumed map there to get a proof of equivalence at that point, and reads the contractibility of the homotopy fibre out of it. removed_items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Theorem 4.6.3 at source lines 571-573: f is an equivalence if and only if it is surjective and an embedding. The author's proof (source lines 574-586) separates the two directions cleanly and the converse is a real argument: surjectivity gives only a truncated inhabitant of the fiber, so after that step the work is to show the fiber is a mere proposition (lines 578-581), and for two fiber elements (x,p) and (y,q) the embedding property produces r : x = y with ap f (r) = p `ct` opp q (lines 582-583), which must then be rearranged by the characterisation of paths in sigma types into the transport statement trans r p = q before r and it can be exhibited as a path in the fiber (lines 584-585). The statement gives no hint that the embedding property is used to produce a path in the source that is then transported.

The author's proof (source lines 617-627) is an explicit quasi-inverse construction rather than a citation: in the case where g o f and g are equivalences it proposes opp(g o f) o g as a quasi-inverse to f (line 618), checks the easy homotopy on A (line 619), and then has to verify the homotopy on B through the three-step chain displayed at lines 620-625 in which the inverse identities of g and of g o f are used in a specific order; the symmetric case, with f o opp(g o f) as a quasi-inverse to g, is stated at line 626. The author's proof (source lines 985-1007) is a chain of reductions in which one link has to be weakened deliberately. Function extensionality is first reduced to the statement that the canonical map from identities of functions to homotopies induces an equivalence on total spaces (source lines 986-994); since the total space on the left is a type of pairs of a section with an identity, contractible by the characterisation of paths with one free endpoint, the goal becomes contractibility of the type of pairs of a section with a pointwise homotopy (source lines 995-999); transposing that type turns it into a product of contractible types, but the transposition result is proved using function extensionality for one of its two composites, so what survives is only a retraction, and the author records explicitly that a retract of a contractible type is contractible (source lines 1000-1006). removed_items.author: The Univalent Foundations Program

removed_items.source_version: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics source tree, file induction.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
removed_items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the unlabelled theorem at source lines 700-702, printed as Theorem 5.5.5: a type satisfies the formation, introduction, elimination and propositional computation rules for W-types exactly when it is a homotopy-initial W-algebra. The author's proof (source lines 705-740) supplies the converse of the preceding homotopy-initiality theorem and does not merely cite it. Assuming that the polynomial functor has a homotopy-initial algebra (W,s_W), the elimination rule is obtained by equipping the Sigma type of pairs (w, c) with c in the assigned family over w with a structure map and applying homotopy-initiality to get a homomorphism whose composite with the first projection must be identified with the identity homomorphism, because the type of endohomomorphisms is contractible; the diagram of that composite is printed in the retained proof (source lines 712-727). The recursor itself is then manufactured by transporting the second component of that homomorphism along the resulting identity in a family of types depending on a function (source lines 729-737), and the computation rule is verified by a calculation with the naturality of those transports (source lines 738-739). The statement indicates neither that the recursor has to be built by transport nor that contractibility of the endohomomorphism type is what makes the two homomorphisms equal.

removed_items.title: Four characterisations of an identity system over a pointed type are logically equivalent
removed_items.author: The Univalent Foundations Program
removed_items.work: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics

removed_items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled theorem at source lines 1152-1160 (book Theorem 5.8.2): four conditions on a pointed predicate over a pointed type, namely being an identity system, having a contractible type of pointed maps into every pointed predicate, having all the transport maps out of the loop space be equivalences, and having a contractible total type, are logically equivalent. The statement lists the four conditions and nothing else, while the proof (source lines 1167-1193) runs the cycle in one direction only and must construct, for each implication, the auxiliary pointed predicate and the two pointed maps that make the argument go through: for the first implication it turns the identity-system elimination into inhabitation and then into a mere proposition by applying elimination to the equality of any two pointed maps; for the second it uses (a_0 = b) as the auxiliary family and gets the composites to be identities from the contractibility of the pointed-map types ppmap(R,R) and ppmap(S,S); the third goes through the equivalence of \Sigma-types; the fourth has to transport the given element along a uniform path family of the contractible total type and check the base-point computation. Only the derived direction of each implication is proved, so the chapter's observation that the four conditions are also logically equivalent as propositions is used, not proved.

removed_items.title: The generating loop of the circle is not the reflexivity path
removed_items.author: The Univalent Foundations Program
removed_items.work: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics
removed_items.source_version: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics source tree, file hits.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
removed_items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source lines 444-446 (book Theorem 6.4.1): the generating loop of the circle is not equal to the reflexivity path at its base point. The statement is a single disequality and the proof (source lines 447-452) has to manufacture the contradiction: it assumes the equality, then uses the recursion principle of the circle to transport that assumption to an arbitrary type carrying an arbitrary loop, concluding that every loop of every type is trivial and therefore that every type is a set, which contradicts the universe not being one. The step from a triviality of one loop to a global triviality of loops is the substance, and the statement contains none of it.
